A1.justification: Both complete 37-page PDFs describe the same ConforMix research. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–H support reliable comparison; all appendix pages are unchanged.

before.justification: v1 reports original conformational-sampling experiments, benchmark comparisons, structural analyses, runtime measurements, and BioEmu free-energy estimation results in Section 4 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results, including benchmark coverage in Tables 1 and 4, runtime and structural-quality measurements, and free-energy convergence in Figure 5.

M1.justification: ConforMix's twisted diffusion sampling, RMSD guidance, secondary-structure masking, filtering, and MBAR reweighting are unchanged. Algorithms 1 and 2 and the BioEmu adaptation in Appendix G are identical.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same domain-motion, membrane-transporter, cryptic-pocket, and fold-switching datasets, alongside the same multichain, RNA, and BioEmu examples. The TP16 attribution changes, but the evaluated 15 transporters and their reference structures remain unchanged.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in Tables 1, 3, and 4 and the supplementary comparisons: default Boltz, AFCluster, CF-random, AFsample2, and BioEmu where applicable. The newly cited Xie and Huang paper is a dataset-source reference, not an added evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: Sampling budgets, baseline MSA modifications, evaluation metrics, filtering thresholds, and BioEmu guidance settings are unchanged in Section 4 and Appendices A, B, D, and G. No experiment or evaluation protocol is added or revised.

E4.justification: The PCA analyses, structural-outlier assessment, filtering analysis, fill-ratio analysis, and biological case studies are retained unchanged, including Table 3 and Figures S3–S11.

E5.justification: Both versions report the same uncertainty procedures: 95% confidence intervals from 1,000 bootstraps in Tables 1 and 4, standard deviations over five runtime runs in Table 2, and 90% intervals from 50 bootstraps in Figure 5.

E6.justification: All numerical results and plotted findings are unchanged across the main text and appendices. For example, Table 1 retains ConforMix's worst-matched coverage of 0.69 ± 0.15 for domain motion and 0.33 ± 0.23 for membrane transporters.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, guidance equations, sampling reasoning, and MBAR derivation in Appendix C are identical. No assumption, proof, or mathematical correction is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contribution statements, and discussion retain the same claims about inference-time conformational exploration, applicability across diffusion models, and faster free-energy estimation.

C2.justification: Interpretations of conformational sampling and baseline performance are unchanged. The same limitations concerning the underlying model landscape, finite-particle sampling, MBAR uncertainty, and preliminary RNA evaluation remain.

D1.justification: Implementation details, hardware, sampling settings, preprocessing descriptions, and code-access information are unchanged. The TP16 edit changes scholarly attribution without revising data-access instructions or experimental implementation.

R1.justification: Section 4.1 changes TP16's attribution from reference [13], Kalakoti and Wallner, to Xie and Huang, adding their 2024 membrane-transporter paper as reference [39]. The former reference [39] becomes [40]. Appendix A still attributes TP16 to [13], leaving the update incomplete.

P1.justification: Edits are confined to the TP16 attribution wording, associated citation numbering, the added bibliography entry, and the arXiv version/date stamp. The narrative, section order, and explanatory prose otherwise remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The added bibliography entry shifts the final reference downward on page 14, and the attribution edit causes local line reflow on page 6. All figures, tables, captions, and their placements remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: The new TP16 reference may improve attribution and traceability, but Section 4.1 now credits Xie and Huang while unchanged Appendix A still credits reference [13]. The supplied PDFs do not resolve these competing attributions, preventing a reliable net quality judgment for this isolated revision. Methods, results, and scientific support are unchanged.
